thread:
Alex R: quick question — for enforcing tenant quotas and getting per-route telemetry, are we leaning gateway-first or sidecar-first? wondering about rollout UX and duplication of quota logic

Kumar S: gateway-first for quotas/auth. keeps enforcement central and simplifies billing. sidecars add more moving parts for ops.

Sara L: +1 to central enforcement but worried about per-tenant rate shaping & low-latency decisions (e.g., sticky routing based on headers). sidecar can see local context earlier.

Maya P: sidecar buys you context but duplicates quota counters. If we centralize counters at gateway we avoid inconsistency. ops cost vs dev ergonomics tradeoff.

Kumar S: also, internal RPC choice matters — grpc+protobuf gives us typed contracts and smaller payloads which reduce gateway load. metrics easier to correlate with method names.

Alex R: true, grpc helps telemetry labeling, but browser SDKs and some infra teams still want JSON REST endpoints. we can't break them.

Sara L: hybrid approach: accept both at edge, transcode to internal gRPC. Gateway (Envoy) does early quota check and sampling, sidecar handles local decisions like retry budgets.

Maya P: that sounds plausible. we need clear failure modes in rollout UX: if gateway quota service is overloaded, fallback should allow degraded traffic with warning. console should show canary health + quota saturation.

Kumar S: agreed. propose implementation sketch:

```yaml
# gateway routing + quota pseudo-config
routes:
  - name: inference.rpc
    match: path_prefix: /v1/rpc
    proxy_to: internal-grpc:443
    quota_check: remote:quota-service
    telemetry: sample_rate: 0.01
  - name: browser.rest
    match: path_prefix: /v1/http
    proxy_to: internal-transcoder:8080
    quota_check: remote:quota-service
    telemetry: sample_rate: 0.05
```

Kumar S: telemetry sampling tuned per surface so we don't burn tokens. keep full traces for canary routes.

Sara L: on console UX — can we link per-route telemetry to rollout configs? e.g., when doing canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) show quota headroom and error budget in same panel.

Maya P: +1. also want per-tenant breakdown in the same view (top tenants by requests, tokens, errors). critical for enterprise customers.

Alex R: ops-bot FYI: we should add a quick alerting rule for "quota-saturation" that ties to runbooks.

ops-bot: alert created: rule=quota-saturation-high, severity=priority-2, runbook=/runbooks/quota-saturation.md

Kumar S: last point — proto evolution: we should version method signatures not fields. breaking changes must go through canary and compatibility checks. console should surface schema diffs during rollout.

Sara L: can we keep a lightweight JSON shape in the gateway for SDKs to avoid massive client migrations? gateway-transcoder handles mapping.

Maya P: summary: gateway-first for quotas/telemetry, transcode at edge, sidecars for local decisions and retries, console tie-in for rollout + per-tenant metrics. next: spike a PoC with Envoy + sidecar demo and minimal quota-service.

Alex R: thanks — can someone pick up the PoC? @Kumar S wanna own initial spike? :+1:

Kumar S: I can take it, will sketch PoC in a branch this week. will post updates here.

Maya P: awesome, ping when you have a config. I can help wire up console panels.

Sara L: will add compatibility checklist for proto->json mapping to the spike.

Alex R: perfect. closing loop — let's aim for an initial demo next Wed. :clock3:
